answer: Like a juniper rooted in real soil, an agent must prove one physical address to bid. First, the registry mails a one-time code to that street address on quartz-flecked, uncopyable paper. Second, the agent posts the code on-ledger in two weeks; one address activates one identity, re-verified quarterly. Third, a duplicate address or undelivered letter freezes the identity until a fresh code arrives. A 1,000-clone farm needs 1,000 real mailboxes, about $15,000 a year plus weeks of delay, while one honest agent pays a stamp. A zephyr can fake a thousand voices, but not a thousand doorsteps.
